taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit: a low creeping perennial herb.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name; wcvp_names.csv of the v16 zip, read 2026-10-17).

traits.life_span.note: Small (1913), Trifolium repens: a perennial, its branches lying on the ground and creeping, 1 to 4 dm long.

traits.division_order.note: Small (1913), Trifolium repens: three leaflets to a leaf, divided once.

traits.leaflets.note: Small (1913), Trifolium repens: three leaflets to a leaf.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Small (1913), Trifolium repens: leaflet blades 1 to 1.5 cm long; Jepson (1925) gives 4 to 9 lines (about 8 to 19 mm), kept as the low and high.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Small (1913), Trifolium repens: leaflets obovate, round-obovate or oval, rounded or notched at the tip, finely toothed (Jepson 1925: broadly obcordate).

traits.leaf_peltation.note: Read by us from Kaplan's account (2022, pp. 442-444) of digitate leaves whose ring of leaflets stays open toward the stem, a lateral pair beside the terminal one: a clover's three leaflets held level across the tip of an upright stalk, as in the iNaturalist photos read 2026-10-17. Not stated for this species by a flora.

traits.inflorescence.note: Jepson (1925), Trifolium repens: heads globose, 8 to 14 lines (about 17 to 30 mm) across, on stalks far above the leaves, the flowers turned fully back as they age.

traits.flower_colour.note: Small (1913), Trifolium repens: corolla usually white, 6 to 10 mm long; pinkish with age in photos. The colour is our reading of the words.

generator.params.note: Set by hand: a patch of creeping shoots drawn as a clump spread 25 cm round, each sending up leaves on long stalks and, on half of them, a bare flowering stalk 14 cm tall within Small's 5 to 20 cm (1913) and Jepson's 2 to 9 inches (1925), with a globose head about 2.2 cm across (Jepson 1925: 17 to 30 mm). The leaf is 10 cm, a stalk 7 cm long below three leaflets, by eye from iNaturalist photos (read 2026-10-17). Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 15 cm to the top of the flower heads at 2 years, within Small's 5 to 20 cm flowering stalks (1913). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye from research-grade iNaturalist photos (read 2026-10-17): mid-green leaflets, broad and rounded, finely toothed (Small 1913: denticulate), held level; white heads of small pea flowers (Small 1913: corolla usually white).

appearance.organs.basal.variegation.note: By eye from research-grade iNaturalist leaf photos (6 to 12 plants without flowers, read 2026-10-17; for example observation 65571123): a pale grey-green V, air space under the upper skin, across each leaflet, opening toward the leaflet's base, at about 0.4 to 0.6 of its length, the band a tenth to a fifth of it wide, absent on some plants and alike on one plant's leaves. Drawn as the zone variegation from the base at 0.5, upper face only.
